item.title: He Once Launched a Grenade for Trump. Now He’ll Be White House Counsel.
item.description: Will Scharf has proved his loyalty to President Trump, even filming a TV ad in which he blows away documents from the president’s legal cases. His new role will be to provide in-house legal advice.
item.dc:creator: Luke Broadwater
item.media:credit: Haiyun Jiang/The New York Times
item.media:description: Will Scharf in the Oval Office earlier this month.

item.title: Trump Administration Wants Billion-Dollar Businesses to Qualify as ‘Small’
item.description: Higher revenue and employee limits for small businesses that get federal contracts and loans could disadvantage the smallest companies, their owners say.
item.dc:creator: Sydney Ember and Lydia DePillis
item.media:credit: Haiyun Jiang for The New York Times
item.media:description: Kelly Loeffler, the head of the Small Business Administration, wants to redefine small businesses.

item.title: Judge Sides With Texas Over Minnesota on Extradition of ICE Agent
item.description: The two states have waged an unusual court battle over the agent facing charges over a shooting in Minneapolis. The agent could be released from jail on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Ernesto Londoño and Mitch Smith
item.media:credit: David Guttenfelder/The New York Times
item.media:description: Federal agents near the scene of a shooting during the Trump administration’s immigration crackdown in January.

item.title: Meta to Pay Up to $17.1 Billion in Landmark Settlement Over Social Media Addiction Claims
item.description: The social media giant settled with 47 states, the District of Columbia and U.S. territories, and agreed to make major changes to its products over claims its platforms endangered children.
item.dc:creator: Cecilia Kang and Eli Tan
item.media:credit: Jason Henry for The New York Times

item.title: After Meta Settlement, Teens Divided on New Instagram and Facebook Restrictions
item.description: Young people said the platforms could be a space for gathering, but also a waste of time.
item.dc:creator: Callie Holtermann and Madison Malone Kircher
item.media:credit: Anna Barclay/Getty Images

item.title: What Does $17.1 Billion Mean for Meta?
item.description: The Silicon Valley company agreed to pay up to $17.1 billion in penalties as part of a landmark settlement with states over social media addiction claims.
item.dc:creator: Emmy Martin
item.media:credit: Jason Henry for The New York Times
item.media:description: Meta’s entire stock value stands at $1.45 trillion. The $17.1 billion penalty is about 1 percent of that.

item.title: Tim Curry, Star of ‘Rocky Horror Picture Show,’ Dies at 80
item.description: The actor’s gift for garish eccentricity was indelibly appropriate for the outlandish, cross-dressing mad scientist Frank-N-Furter.
item.dc:creator: Bruce Weber
item.media:credit: Evening Standard/Hulton Archive, via Getty Images
item.media:description: Tim Curry in 1974, the year he starred in the premiere American production of “The Rocky Horror Show” in Los Angeles.

item.title: Tim Curry Pioneered Fashion With His ‘Rocky Horror’ Performance
item.description: His performance as Frank-N-Furter, the cross-dressing mad scientist of “The Rocky Horror Picture Show,” was ahead of its time.

item.title: Tim Curry: A Life in Pictures

item.title: Judge Allows Postal Service Effort to Restrict Mail Voting, for Now
item.description: The order came amid a spate of legal challenges, including one by Democratic state attorneys general, that could still result in the rules being blocked.
item.dc:creator: Zach Montague
item.media:credit: Philip Cheung for The New York Times
item.media:description: Under its new plan, the Postal Service would not deliver mail ballots in states that do not share voter data with the agency and would deliver only ballots that meet certain criteria.

item.title: Maryland Judge Blocks Democratic Redistricting Measure
item.description: A judge found that Democratic lawmakers had not followed proper procedures in passing a redistricting amendment, but the state Supreme Court will have the final say.
item.dc:creator: Campbell Robertson
item.media:credit: Michelle Gustafson for The New York Times
item.media:description: The Maryland State House in downtown Annapolis.

item.title: Where Does Trump’s Effort to Restrict Mail Voting Stand?
item.description: The Supreme Court on Monday allowed the Trump administration to continue with plans to curtail mail-in voting, but the fast-moving, high-stakes legal fight continues.
item.dc:creator: Adam Sella and Abbie VanSickle
item.media:credit: Philip Cheung for The New York Times
item.media:description: President Trump has long made unfounded claims that mail voting is fraudulent and corrupt, even as he has cast his own ballots by mail in multiple elections.

item.title: The South Loved Dolly Parton. It Saw the Best of Itself in Her.
item.description: Even as her talents and work ethic opened up the world to her, she kept coming home. For many in the complicated region she’s from, that meant a lot.
item.dc:creator: Rick Rojas and Emily Cochrane
item.media:credit: Will Crooks for The New York Times

item.title: Dolly Parton’s Other Legacy: A Fortune Given Away, Dollar by Dollar
item.description: The country star supported early childhood literacy, disaster relief, the development of the Covid-19 vaccine and more.
item.dc:creator: David Gelles
item.media:credit: Andrew Harnik/Associated Press
item.media:description: Dolly Parton spoke at the Library of Congress during a 2018 celebration of her organization, the Imagination Library, and its 100 millionth book donation.

item.title: Meet Dean Roy, the 15-Year-Old Running for Vermont Governor and Ready for ‘Impact’
item.description: Dean Roy, 15, will appear on the ballot in November as a third-party candidate. He said his generation’s concerns, like affordability and climate change, have been ignored for too long.
item.dc:creator: Pooja Salhotra
item.media:credit: Anna Watts for The New York Times
item.media:description: “The goal here is to make enough of an impact that the leaders have to start paying attention to the youth voice,” Dean Roy said.

item.title: How Darline Graham’s Politics Compare With Her Brother’s as She Runs for Senate
item.description: Senator Darline Graham has spoken far more about her desire to support President Trump’s agenda than she has talked about her brother’s political goals — or her own.
item.dc:creator: Bayliss Wagner
item.media:credit: Haiyun Jiang/The New York Times
item.media:description: Ms. Graham has said she wants government to help people no longer rely on Social Security.

item.title: F.D.A. Approves the Drug Daraxonrasib That’s Poised to Transform Pancreatic Cancer
item.description: In a key clinical trial, patients who got the pill, daraxonrasib, lived twice as long as those who got chemotherapy.
item.dc:creator: Gina Kolata, Rebecca Robbins and Carolyn Y. Johnson
item.media:credit: Kim Raff for The New York Times
item.media:description: Daraxonrasib, the first drug of its type, has electrified pancreatic cancer specialists and patients because it has shown it can double life expectancy.

item.title: Did the Zodiac Kill the Black Dahlia? This Crime Writer Thinks So.
item.description: The novelist Michael Connelly knows he is putting his reputation on the line with the podcast “Killer in the Code.” But despite critics’ skepticism, he finds the evidence “completely convincing.”

item.media:credit: Philip Cheung for The New York Times
item.media:description: Michael Connelly, a reporter turned novelist, has created iconic characters like Harry Bosch and Mickey Haller, otherwise known as the Lincoln Lawyer.

item.title: Summer Weather in L.A. Was Perfect. Then Came Humidity and Mosquitoes.

item.media:credit: Ariana Drehsler for The New York Times
item.media:description: Meteorologists don’t track humidity as closely as they do temperature, but trends point to stickier air than usual in coastal Southern California.
